beatbox.foundations.lede: Four grounds, one accent, three faces and one shape. Every screen is assembled out of this page, and this page is rendered from the tokens themselves — so if it looks right, they are right.
beatbox.foundations.menu.note: Every closed question in BeatBox is this control. The list is drawn by the page, not by GTK: a raised list, a neutral highlight under the pointer, a check on what is chosen, and arrows, Enter, Escape and typing a letter all work. An option may carry a sign before it and a hint after it; a value no longer on offer is shown and marked, never blanked.
beatbox.foundations.menu.stale: A value no longer on offer
beatbox.foundations.motion_note: Motion belongs to something that changes while you are watching it: a total on a screen that has just opened, a selection moving to where you put it. A tier's label and a count that has not changed never animate — a property that animates is claiming to be an event. Both pieces here are adapted from React Bits and rebuilt on this palette; the chip row's droplets are the pill's own white, and the counter brings no animation library with it.
beatbox.foundations.number.note: Every number in BeatBox that a person types is this control, never the platform spinner: its two white wedges are painted by the OS, sit on the text and ignore the palette. Typing, the arrow keys and the wheel still work, because it is a real number input underneath. The two steps live in their own raised cells after a hairline, a minus and a plus in the same muted ink as the rest, with a neutral hover and no violet. At the limit a step dims instead of vanishing, so the field never changes width. Out of range turns the border rose. Ports are the first user; durations and counts adopt it unchanged.
beatbox.foundations.shape_note: One isometric cube at four tints and one wireframe state. It is a machine: the node in a topology, the way in on Account, the empty screens — never redrawn, only re-tinted. The mark is the logo, the same cube taken apart, and it is always violet.
beatbox.foundations.type_note: Sora carries the voice, Plex Sans carries the reading, Plex Mono carries anything a machine produced — an IP, a port, a digest, a path, a timer. If digits line up in a column they are mono and tabular; if they sit in a sentence they never are.
beatbox.foundations.verdict_note: Semantic colour never borrows the accent. ALLOWED is rose because in a sandbox reachable is the finding; INSUFFICIENT has no tint because it is not a verdict at all, and colouring it would rank it against answers it cannot be compared to.

beatbox.net.keep.old_daemon: The engine is older than this window. Restart BeatBox to keep networks.
beatbox.net.keep.title: Keep this network
beatbox.net.keep.vms_stay: Connected VMs do not go back; only the network does. Conversations and leases start over.
beatbox.net.lab.dmz.what: A DMZ facing the internet, the inside hidden, IPv6.
beatbox.net.lab.empty.what: Just the router. You draw the rest.
beatbox.net.lab.expects: It expects virtual machines called {names}: cable them in afterwards.
beatbox.net.lab.expects_one: It expects a virtual machine called {names}: cable one in afterwards.
beatbox.net.lab.home.what: One router, NAT and the internet. Everything on one network.
beatbox.net.lab.sites.what: Two routers, routes, and the branch hidden behind NAT.
beatbox.net.lab.switches.what: No router in the way: two VLANs that never talk to each other.
beatbox.net.lab.vlans.what: Management, Sales and Servers on the same cable.
beatbox.net.limit.all_what: counted for all of them together
beatbox.net.limit.only_allow: Only a rule that allows can have a pace.
beatbox.net.limit.title: Pace
beatbox.net.limit.what: It counts new connections, not packets: an SSH session already open does not use it up. “Each machine”: each has its own; “all together”: the rule has one.
beatbox.net.lookups.most: {percent}% of every ask is {node} asking for {name}. Harmless — it just never gets an answer here.
beatbox.net.lookups.title: Names looked up
beatbox.net.lookups.what_short: To answer a name here, add it under Names and addresses. Other names go outside only when Internet is on.
beatbox.net.names.about: The router gives each machine of {name} an address and answers for the names. What runs inside a machine stays in the Server.
beatbox.net.names.before: It goes in after the other rules by name, before the rules by address.
beatbox.net.names.first: They come before the rules by address
beatbox.net.names.name: Name
beatbox.net.names.star: *.example.com is example.com itself and everything that ends in it (www., m., …).
beatbox.net.names.title: Sites and names
beatbox.net.names.what_each: Hide: the router says the name does not exist. Send to: the name becomes another machine. Cut the site: the connection is cut when the browser says the name, even if the machine found the address some other way.
beatbox.net.nat.forwards_note: What arrives at a port goes to a machine
beatbox.net.nat.forwards_what: A hidden network takes only answers. A forward opens one port of the router to one machine behind it.
beatbox.net.nat.inside_only: Only what is already inside the lab gets here (another network, another router). Nothing opens on your computer.
beatbox.net.nat.shown_what: Its machines are seen as they are
beatbox.net.new.cidr_from_lab: The lab's range. Change it and the machines on it, its names and rules move with it; VLANs keep their own.
beatbox.net.new.cidr_hint: The first is the gateway; machines get theirs from .10 up.
beatbox.net.new.name: Name
beatbox.net.new.title: New network
beatbox.net.new.what: A network is a router, and the switches you add, inside BeatBox itself: no privilege, and it costs nothing while idle. Either start can be changed later.
beatbox.net.nodes.none: Nothing is cabled to it yet.
beatbox.net.nodes.stop_first: Stop {name} first: a machine's card changes only while it is off.
beatbox.net.overview.about: How {name} is, and what it has counted.
beatbox.net.path.routed: The router {device} took it in on VLAN {vlan} and sent it on to VLAN {out}.
beatbox.net.path.router: The router {device} took it in on VLAN {vlan}.
beatbox.net.path.switch: The switch {device} took it in on port {port}, in VLAN {vlan}.
beatbox.net.picture.title: What is plugged in
beatbox.net.policy.allow.what: Everything may talk until a rule says no.
beatbox.net.policy.deny.what: Nothing may talk until a rule says yes. Answers still come back.
beatbox.net.range.after: Done. Turn the machines on again: each takes its new address when it starts.
beatbox.net.range.blocked_machines: Turn off {names} first: a machine that is on keeps its old address.
beatbox.net.range.hint: The machines, names and rules that mention the old range move with it.
beatbox.net.range.kept: Left as they are, because the new range has no place for them: {list}.
beatbox.net.range.unchanged: Not changed: addresses fixed inside a machine, and anything that carries an address of its own.
beatbox.net.router.design.about: Its networks, the paths between them and the firewall. The addresses it hands out and the names it answers are under Names and addresses.
beatbox.net.router.design.internet_what: Names, TCP and UDP pass. Ping to the internet is not supported yet.
beatbox.net.router.design.main_internet: Only {router}, the main router, connects to the internet. This router reaches it through its routes.
beatbox.net.router.design.networks_what: A VLAN only gives machines addresses when the router has a network in it. {firewall} decides what passes between them.
beatbox.net.router.design.no_router: No router yet. Add one on the Overview page.
beatbox.net.router.title: Router
beatbox.net.routes.none: No routes: it reaches only its own networks.
beatbox.net.routes.title: Routes
beatbox.net.routes.what: Where this router sends what is on none of its own networks: everything in a range goes through a neighbouring router.
beatbox.net.rule.deny_reject: Block: the packet vanishes and whoever asked waits. Reject: they hear “no” at once.
beatbox.net.rule.only_new_what: New only: the rule leaves answers alone.
beatbox.net.rule.other_what: Any IP protocol by name or number (gre, esp, 47), ICMP with its type, and outside IP an EtherType (0x88cc).
beatbox.net.rule.pick_other: Pick “Something else…” after “by” to give a protocol and ports.
beatbox.net.services.title: Services
beatbox.net.services.what: Names for what rules say after “by”.
beatbox.net.story.noise: Besides that, the operating systems announced themselves {count} times — normal chatter.
beatbox.net.story.noise_blocked: Besides that, the operating systems announced themselves {count} times — normal chatter, blocked by the default rule.
beatbox.net.story.outside: {count} names outside this network were looked up and not found: it has no way out.
beatbox.net.story.quiet: Your machines have not talked to each other yet.
beatbox.net.sure.destroy.what: Its machines are unplugged and left with no network.
beatbox.net.sure.reset: Put {name} back as it was made?
beatbox.net.sure.reset.what: Rules, names and traffic go back; the machines stay cabled. It stops until you start it again.
beatbox.net.switch.title: Switch
beatbox.net.test.by_reject: Rule {n} rejects it: they hear “no” at once.
beatbox.net.test.cut: Cut by {rule} when the connection says the name, whatever the rules by address say.
beatbox.net.test.cut_unsaid: Only the web and secure web say the name, so {rule} does not cut this connection.
beatbox.net.test.default_allow: No rule fits; the default lets it through.
beatbox.net.test.default_deny: No rule fits; the default blocks it.
beatbox.net.test.found_gateway: Found the usual way: the router, {address}.
beatbox.net.test.found_machine: Found the usual way: the machine {machine}, {address}.
beatbox.net.test.found_record: Found the usual way, under Names and addresses: {address}.
beatbox.net.test.hidden: Hidden by {rule}: the router says the name does not exist.
beatbox.net.test.name: The name the machine asks for
beatbox.net.test.no_address: The machine never learns an address.
beatbox.net.test.outside: Nothing here has this name, so it is asked of the internet.
beatbox.net.test.same_machine: The name leads back to the machine that asks.
beatbox.net.test.sent_nowhere: Sent to {to} by {rule}, but nothing here has that name.
beatbox.net.test.title: Would it get through?
beatbox.net.test.two: It takes two machines on this network to ask.
beatbox.net.test.type_name: Write the name the machine asks for.
beatbox.net.test.unknown: Nothing here has this name, and the router does not lead to the internet.
beatbox.net.topo.no_network_why: The router has no address in VLAN {vlan}, so this machine gets none.
beatbox.net.topo.no_router_why: Its VLAN never reaches the router, so it gets no address. Put the ports on the way in the same VLAN, or use a trunk.
beatbox.net.traffic.bandwidth_kbps.what: How much fits through at once
beatbox.net.traffic.latency_ms.what: How long each packet waits, each way
beatbox.net.traffic.lede: How the cable between the machines behaves. A change takes effect at once, for every machine on this network. A single cable can add its own on top, from the Overview.
beatbox.net.traffic.pending: Not in force until you apply it.
beatbox.net.vlans.moved: {node} moves from {from} to {to}. It takes the new address when it next renews (usually within five minutes, ten at most), or when it restarts.
beatbox.net.vlans.title: Networks by VLAN
beatbox.net.way.blocked_what: The router's firewall let it go unanswered. {to} never knew.
beatbox.net.way.by_default_what: When no rule fits, the firewall blocks.
beatbox.net.way.closed_what: It stopped at {router}'s door: the network behind it is hidden, and takes only answers. {to} never knew.
beatbox.net.way.cut_what: The router cut it when it asked for {name}: {to} saw it begin, never what it asked.
beatbox.net.way.forward_what: It reached {router} at port {port} and was sent on to {to}, port {to_port}.
beatbox.net.way.hidden_what: {to} did not see {from}: it saw the router {router}.
beatbox.net.way.no_router: It stayed inside a switch: it never crossed a router, so there is no way to draw.
beatbox.net.way.refused_what: The router's firewall said no at once. {to} never knew.
beatbox.net.way.said_no_what: {to} said no: nothing on it listens on port {port}.
beatbox.net.way.silent_what: {to} did not answer: it may be busy, or its own firewall keeps quiet.
beatbox.network.address_outside: {address} cannot be given out on {cidr}: it is outside it, or it is the network's own, its gateway's or its broadcast address.
beatbox.network.address_taken: {address} is already somebody's on this network.
beatbox.network.bad_cidr: '{cidr}' cannot be a network. Use a range like 10.10.10.0/24 (from /8 to /29).
beatbox.network.bad_device: '{device}' cannot name a device: lowercase letters, digits, - and _, starting with a letter, 32 at most.
beatbox.network.bad_dns_name: '{name}' cannot be a DNS name: letters, digits, - and _, between dots.
beatbox.network.bad_file: This file is not a BeatBox network.
beatbox.network.bad_forward: A forward needs TCP or UDP, a router port, a machine and its port ({field}).
beatbox.network.bad_group: '{group}' cannot be a group name: up to 24 characters, no ':'.
beatbox.network.bad_lease: {seconds} s is out of range. Use one minute to one day.
beatbox.network.bad_name: There is no name '{name}' to change here.
beatbox.network.bad_node: '{node}' cannot be a name. Use lowercase letters, digits, - and _, starting with a letter, up to 32.
beatbox.network.bad_pool: {first} to {last} is not a part of this network that can be handed out.
beatbox.network.bad_service: '{service}' cannot be a service: up to 24 characters, no ':', and a protocol.
beatbox.network.bad_vlan: '{vlan}' is not a VLAN: a number from 1 to 4094.
beatbox.network.bad_vlan_name: A VLAN's name is up to 24 characters, with no control characters.
beatbox.network.capture_failed: The capture could not be written: {error}
beatbox.network.capture_running: That cable is already being captured.
beatbox.network.device_kind: A device is a switch or a router.
beatbox.network.device_taken: Something on this network is already called {device}.
beatbox.network.export_failed: The file could not be written: {error}
beatbox.network.file_too_new: This network was saved by a newer BeatBox.
beatbox.network.forward_taken: That port on the router already leads somewhere: {port}.
beatbox.network.full: {cidr} has no address left to give.
beatbox.network.group_in_use: Rule {n} names the group {group}: remove the rule first.
beatbox.network.isolated.what: A card and an address, and everything it sends outward is dropped.
beatbox.network.last_router: The router is the network's gateway: its addresses, names and firewall. It cannot be taken away.
beatbox.network.light_off: {node} only runs while the network does: start the network first.
beatbox.network.loop: That cable would close a loop: there is already a way between those two devices. Take another cable out first.
beatbox.network.main_vlan: VLAN 1 is the router's main network: use Change the range on the Router page.
beatbox.network.nat.what: A route out to the internet. Not for anything you do not trust.
beatbox.network.nat_shared: {router} reaches another router through VLAN {vlan}: hiding it would cut the routes between them.
beatbox.network.no_such_cable: There is no cable on that port.
beatbox.network.no_such_device: There is no such device on this network.
beatbox.network.no_such_interface: The router has no network in VLAN {vlan}.
beatbox.network.no_such_job: There is no answer waiting for job {job}: it was taken already, or it is too old.
beatbox.network.no_such_node: Nothing called {node} is cabled to this network.
beatbox.network.none.what: No card at all. Nothing to reach and nothing to be reached from.
beatbox.network.not_on_this_system: Network sandboxes run on Linux for now.
beatbox.network.overlap: {cidr} shares addresses with {other}, another of the router's networks. Pick a range of its own.
beatbox.network.path_too_long: The network's folder path is too long ({path}). Move it somewhere shorter.
beatbox.network.port_taken: That port already has something plugged into it. Choose a free one.
beatbox.network.rename_machine: {node} is a virtual machine: it is called what the machine is called. Rename the machine itself.
beatbox.network.renumber_mismatch: Only the range may change, and the names and rules that mention it have to move with it. Ask for the plan and apply what it says.
beatbox.network.renumber_same: That is the range this network already has.
beatbox.network.route_via: {via} is not on any of {router}'s networks: a route's next hop has to be a neighbour.
beatbox.pen.about: Take files from this computer into {name}, as if you plugged in a pen drive. It can only read them — it can never change or delete your files.
beatbox.pen.how: Choose a folder on this computer: everything in it shows up inside the machine as a pen drive called “BEATBOX PEN”. Up to 500 MB.
beatbox.pen.in: Plugged in, with this folder on it:
beatbox.pen.inside: Inside the machine it is the pen drive called “BEATBOX PEN”. If it does not open by itself, look for it in the file manager.
beatbox.pen.not_this_one: A machine marked as dangerous cannot take a pen.
beatbox.pen.off: {name} is off. Start it to plug in a pen.
beatbox.pen.pick: Choose the folder to put on the pen
beatbox.pen.safe: Read-only: the machine can look at these files and copy them, but nothing it does can change or delete them on this computer.
beatbox.pen.title: The pen
beatbox.plain.boundary.container: It has its own view of this computer, but shares its kernel.
beatbox.plain.boundary.machine: It has a kernel of its own, so nothing running in it is running on this computer.
beatbox.plain.boundary.none: It shares this computer — there is no boundary around it.
beatbox.plain.is.destroyed: Thrown away. Its disk went with it.
beatbox.plain.reach.isolated: and a network it cannot get out of.
beatbox.plain.reach.nat: and a way out to the internet.
beatbox.plain.reach.network: and a cable to a BeatBox network, as {address}.
beatbox.plain.reach.none: and no way to reach anything.
beatbox.plain.sure.destroy.what: {name} and its disk go for good. The disk you gave it is not touched.
beatbox.plain.sure.reset.what: Everything {name} has done since it was made goes, including its save points. The disk you gave it is not touched.
beatbox.plain.why.bad_save_name: A save point cannot be called that. Leave out quotes and backslashes.
beatbox.plain.why.blank: Something that had to be filled in was left blank.
beatbox.plain.why.broke: Something went wrong underneath. The Engine screen has the detail.
beatbox.plain.why.delete_failed: The save point {name} could not be deleted: {detail}
beatbox.plain.why.disk_in_the_way: There is already something where this machine's disk would go.
beatbox.plain.why.disk_in_use: A machine is still using that disk. Throw the machine away first.
beatbox.plain.why.fixed_setting: That cannot change on a machine that already exists. Make a new one instead.
beatbox.plain.why.gone: This machine has been thrown away.
beatbox.plain.why.guest_lost: BeatBox lost this machine while it was closed. Start it again, or throw it away.
beatbox.plain.why.hostile_with_a_way_out: Something marked as dangerous cannot be given a way out to the internet.
beatbox.plain.why.install_unfinished: The install did not finish, so nothing on the disk can start. Install again.
beatbox.plain.why.no_agent: Nothing inside is answering. Wait a minute; if it keeps saying this, install the guest agent on its disk.
beatbox.plain.why.no_disk: This machine has nothing to boot. Give it a disk you already have.
beatbox.plain.why.no_disk_made: BeatBox could not give this machine a disk of its own.
beatbox.plain.why.no_disk_there: The disk is not there: {path}. Reconnect the drive, then try again.
beatbox.plain.why.no_display: QEMU cannot show a window here. Install its display: {install}
beatbox.plain.why.no_file: There is no such file inside the machine.
beatbox.plain.why.no_qemu: QEMU is not installed, so no machine can run. Install it in Setup.
beatbox.plain.why.no_room: There is not enough left on this computer for a machine that size.
beatbox.plain.why.no_save_point: There is no save point by that name.
beatbox.plain.why.no_such_disk: That disk is not there any more.
beatbox.plain.why.no_uefi: This machine needs UEFI firmware for QEMU (OVMF). Install it with: {command}
beatbox.plain.why.no_uefi_vars: The machine's UEFI settings could not be made: {detail}
beatbox.plain.why.not_a_disk: This does not read as a disk: {detail}
beatbox.plain.why.not_enough_memory: It wants {wanted} GB and only {free} GB are free. Give it less, or close something first.
beatbox.plain.why.not_now: Not while the machine is like this.
beatbox.plain.why.nothing_installed: Nothing was installed: it closed before the installer wrote anything. Make it again and choose “Install” inside.
beatbox.plain.why.out_of_memory: This computer ran out of memory and switched it off. Close something or give it less, then start it again.
beatbox.plain.why.ova_compressed: This .ova's disk is compressed. Export it again from VirtualBox without compression.
beatbox.plain.why.ova_is_an_archive: An .ova is a package. New machine can take the disk out of it.
beatbox.plain.why.ova_without_disk: There is no disk inside this .ova.
beatbox.plain.why.restore_failed: Could not go back to {name}, so it was turned off. It was probably saved with other hardware, like another network. ({detail})
beatbox.plain.why.save_failed: The save point could not be taken: {detail}
beatbox.plain.why.setup_differs: {name} was saved when {setting} was {was}; now it is {now}. Stop the machine, set it back, then go back.
beatbox.plain.why.shut_down: It was shut down from inside. Start it again whenever you like.
beatbox.plain.why.state_saved: State saved: it carries on from here.
beatbox.plain.why.still_going: It is still running inside. Nothing was stopped.
beatbox.plain.why.stopped_after_failed_r: Going back to {name} failed, so it was turned off. Start it again: it boots from {name}'s disk.
beatbox.plain.why.too_few_cpus: A machine needs at least one processor.
beatbox.plain.why.too_little_memory: That is not enough memory to boot anything.
beatbox.plain.why.tools_download_failed: The guest tools did not download. Check you are online and try again.
beatbox.plain.why.tools_not_here: The guest tools are not on this computer yet.
beatbox.plain.why.tools_wrong_file: The download was not the right file, so it was thrown away. Try again later.
beatbox.plain.why.uefi_gone: The UEFI firmware at {path} is not there any more.
beatbox.plain.why.unknown: That did not work. The Engine screen says exactly why.
beatbox.plain.why.unknown_kind: BeatBox does not know how to make that kind of machine.
beatbox.plain.why.unpack_failed: The disk could not be taken out: {detail}
beatbox.plain.why.unreadable_disk: That file cannot be read as a disk.
beatbox.plain.why.virtualbox_difference: This is a VirtualBox snapshot file. Choose the machine's main disk, or clone it in VirtualBox (Clone → Current state).
beatbox.plain.why.went_away: The machine went away on its own.
beatbox.probe.frida.missing: frida was not found; it comes with frida-tools
beatbox.probe.frida.ready: frida {version} — the guest still needs frida-server in its own image
beatbox.probe.kvm.missing: No /dev/kvm, so machines run much slower. Turn on virtualization in the firmware, or load the kvm module.
beatbox.probe.kvm.no_permission: You cannot open /dev/kvm, so machines run about ten times slower. Run sudo usermod -aG kvm $USER, then log out and back in.
beatbox.probe.kvm.not_linux: KVM is Linux-only. A guest still runs here, just without hardware acceleration.
beatbox.probe.kvm.ready: /dev/kvm is present and this user can open it
beatbox.probe.kvm.whpx_missing: the Windows Hypervisor Platform is off, so machines run about ten times slower. Turn it on in “Turn Windows features on or off” and restart.
beatbox.probe.kvm.whpx_ready: the Windows Hypervisor Platform is on, so guests run on Windows' own hypervisor
beatbox.probe.qemu.missing: qemu-system-x86_64 was not found, so no machine can start. Install QEMU, or point BEATBOX_QEMU_DIR at one.
beatbox.probe.terminal.no_pty: a real terminal needs a pty, and pty is POSIX-only
beatbox.processes.end_sure: End {name}? Anything unsaved in it is lost.
beatbox.reach.isolated.what: A card, and nothing it sends gets out.
beatbox.reach.nat.what: A real way out. Not for anything you distrust.
beatbox.reach.network.what: A cable to one of your networks, and nothing past it.
beatbox.sandbox.can_nothing: This sandbox declared no capabilities, so there is nothing to ask it.
beatbox.sandbox.form.agent: Talk to a guest agent inside
beatbox.sandbox.form.agent_hint: Running a command or reading a file needs qemu-guest-agent on the disk. Without it the sandbox still works, and simply does not offer those.
beatbox.sandbox.form.disk_hint: A disk you already have. BeatBox never downloads one, and never writes to this file — the sandbox gets an overlay of its own.
beatbox.sandbox.form.name: Name
beatbox.sandbox.look_hint: Asks the guest what is true now. Nothing here refreshes on its own.
beatbox.sandbox.none: No sandboxes yet. Make one and it appears here, with everything it says.
beatbox.sandbox.not_running: It has to be running before anything can be asked of it.
beatbox.sandbox.pick_one: Pick a sandbox on the right.
beatbox.say.detail.busy: it is in use by something else
beatbox.say.detail.not_found: the file or folder does not exist
beatbox.say.detail.port_busy: the port is already taken by another program
beatbox.say.detail.read_only: that place can only be read, not written
beatbox.say.detail.refused: nothing was listening on the other side
beatbox.say.detail.timeout: it did not answer in time
beatbox.say.detail.unreachable: there is no way to it on the network
beatbox.say.unknown: Something went wrong. Close BeatBox and open it again; if it keeps happening, the engine's log has the details.
beatbox.screen.account.blurb: Guest is ready now. Accounts come later.
beatbox.screen.account.title: Pick a way in.

A debugger, not the product — the Sandbox screen is that.
beatbox.screen.engine.title: Engine
beatbox.screen.foundations.blurb: The tokens, the scale, the shape and the bridge — the system every other screen is built from.
beatbox.screen.foundations.title: Foundations
beatbox.screen.hero.blurb: The way in: what BeatBox is for, and the one button that opens the sandbox.
beatbox.screen.hero.title: Break the box.
beatbox.screen.host.commands.blurb: Run things inside a machine without touching its screen.
beatbox.screen.host.commands.title: Commands
beatbox.screen.host.machine.blurb: A machine of your own, with a kernel of its own, that you can throw away. Point BeatBox at a disk you already have; it never writes to it.
beatbox.screen.host.machine.title: Machines
beatbox.screen.host.pen.blurb: Take files from this computer into the machine, as if you plugged in a pen drive. The machine can only read it — it can never change or delete your files.
beatbox.screen.host.pen.title: USB drive
beatbox.screen.host.watchers.blurb: Commands that keep running inside a machine, and tell you when something changes.
beatbox.screen.host.watchers.title: Watchers

beatbox.screen.network.firewall.title: Firewall
beatbox.screen.network.flows.blurb: Every conversation on a network, as it happens.
beatbox.screen.network.flows.title: Flows
beatbox.screen.network.names.blurb: The addresses each network hands out and the names its routers answer.
beatbox.screen.network.names.title: Names and addresses
beatbox.screen.network.overview.blurb: A network of your own: how it is and what it has counted.
beatbox.screen.network.overview.title: Overview
beatbox.screen.network.router.blurb: The device a network's machines leave by: networks, routes, firewall.
beatbox.screen.network.router.title: Router
beatbox.screen.network.traffic.blurb: Latency, loss and bandwidth on a network.
beatbox.screen.network.traffic.title: Traffic
beatbox.screen.server.library.blurb: The kinds of service the server can put to work, and yours.
beatbox.screen.server.library.title: Library
beatbox.screen.server.services.blurb: What the server puts to work for the network: a website, names for the machines, a service of your own.
beatbox.screen.server.services.title: Services
beatbox.screen.server.settings.blurb: The server itself: where it is and what it does when it starts.
beatbox.screen.server.settings.title: Configuration
beatbox.screen.server.try.blurb: See whether the services work from another machine, and ask them what they can do.
beatbox.screen.server.try.title: Try it
beatbox.screen.settings.blurb: How BeatBox behaves, what this computer can give it, and where it keeps things.
beatbox.screen.settings.title: Settings
beatbox.screen.setup.blurb: What BeatBox needs from this computer, and whether it is here. Anything missing that BeatBox can put in place itself has a button; the system asks for your password or approval, never BeatBox.
